032/**
033 * The configuration of a RainbowGum. In some other logging implementations this is called
034 * "context".
035 * <p>
036 * A config can be used by only one {@link RainbowGum}, even after that RainbowGum is
037 * closed. Using it for another {@link RainbowGum.Builder} throws
038 * {@link IllegalStateException}; build a new config instead.
039 */
040public sealed interface LogConfig extends LogProperty.PropertySupport {
041
042        /**
043         * When to dump bootstrap alerts to the fail-safe output.
044         */
045        public enum DebugModeType {
046
047                /**
048                 * Do not dump alerts beyond the normal alert startup policy.
049                 */
050                @EnumAlias("false")
051                OFF,
052                /**
053                 * Dump the failure and collected alerts if building the config fails.
054                 */
055                ERROR,
056                /**
057                 * Dump collected alerts after every successful config build and on build failure.
058                 */
059                INFO,
060                /**
061                 * Dump collected alerts as in {@link #INFO}, and print a {@link LogReporter}
062                 * report after Rainbow Gum starts.
063                 */
064                @EnumAlias("true")
065                ALL,
066                /**
067                 * Everything {@link #ALL} does, then fails after Rainbow Gum starts if a property
068                 * key set in a source that can list its keys (system properties, property files)
069                 * was never read and is close to a key that was, which is almost always a typo.
070                 * Meant for trying configuration on the command line and in CI.
071                 */
072                HELP;
073
074                boolean checksUnusedKeys() {
075                        return this == ALL || this == HELP;
076                }
077
078                static DebugModeType parse(String value) {
079                        String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
080                        return switch (v) {
081                                case "FALSE" -> OFF;
082                                case "TRUE" -> ALL;
083                                default -> LogProperty.enumValue(DebugModeType.class, value, "true", "false");
084                        };
085                }
086
087        }
088

174        /**

181        /**
182         * Settings that apply to the whole configuration rather than to one component. Each
183         * is set with a {@link Builder} method and overridden by its property when present.
184         */
185        public final class Globals {
186
187                private final ChangeMode changeMode;
188
189                private final AnsiMode ansiMode;
190
191                private final AppenderLock appenderLock;
192
193                private final ThreadLocalMode threadLocal;
194
195                private final boolean optimize;
196
197                private final Set<LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source> keyValueSources;
198
199                Globals(ChangeMode changeMode, AnsiMode ansiMode, AppenderLock appenderLock, ThreadLocalMode threadLocal,
200                                boolean optimize, Set<LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source> keyValueSources) {
201                        this.changeMode = changeMode;
202                        this.ansiMode = ansiMode;
203                        this.appenderLock = appenderLock;
204                        this.threadLocal = threadLocal;
205                        this.optimize = optimize;
206                        this.keyValueSources = Set.copyOf(keyValueSources);
207                }
208
209                /**
210                 * Whether loggers can change at runtime, from
211                 * {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY}.
212                 * @return change mode.
213                 */
214                public ChangeMode changeMode() {
215                        return changeMode;
216                }
217
218                /**
219                 * Whether output uses ANSI escape codes, from
220                 * {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_ANSI_MODE_PROPERTY}.
221                 * @return ANSI mode.
222                 */
223                public AnsiMode ansiMode() {
224                        return ansiMode;
225                }
226
227                /**
228                 * Which kind of lock appenders use, from
229                 * {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_LOCK_PROPERTY}.
230                 * @return appender lock.
231                 */
232                public AppenderLock appenderLock() {
233                        return appenderLock;
234                }
235
236                /**
237                 * Whether the logging path may use a {@link ThreadLocal}, from
238                 * {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_THREAD_LOCAL_PROPERTY}.
239                 * @return thread local mode.
240                 */
241                public ThreadLocalMode threadLocal() {
242                        return threadLocal;
243                }
244
245                /**
246                 * Whether unset appender and encoder choices use what is best for the platform,
247                 * from {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY}.
248                 * @return true if optimizing.
249                 */
250                public boolean optimize() {
251                        return optimize;
252                }
253
254                /**
255                 * Key value sources whose contributors add key values to events, from
256                 * {@value LogProperties#KEY_VALUES_SOURCES_PROPERTY}.
257                 * @return selected sources.
258                 */
259                public Set<LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source> keyValueSources() {
260                        return keyValueSources;
261                }
262
263                /*
264                 * Every property is checked before any error is thrown, so all mistakes are
265                 * reported together.
266                 */
267                Globals withProperties(LogProperties properties) {
268                        var validator = LogProperty.Validator.of(LogConfig.class);
269                        var change = properties.forKey(LogProperties.CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY)
270                                .ofString()
271                                .map(ChangeMode::parse)
272                                .or(changeMode)
273                                .validateIfError(validator);
274                        var ansi = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_ANSI_MODE_PROPERTY)
275                                .ofString()
276                                .map(AnsiMode::parse)
277                                .or(ansiMode)
278                                .validateIfError(validator);
279                        var lock = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_APPENDER_LOCK_PROPERTY)
280                                .ofString()
281                                .map(v -> LogProperty.enumValue(AppenderLock.class, v))
282                                .or(appenderLock)
283                                .validateIfError(validator);
284                        var threadLocalMode = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_THREAD_LOCAL_PROPERTY)
285                                .ofString()
286                                .map(v -> LogProperty.enumValue(ThreadLocalMode.class, v))
287                                .or(threadLocal)
288                                .validateIfError(validator);
289                        var opt = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY)
290                                .ofBoolean()
291                                .or(optimize)
292                                .validateIfError(validator);
293                        var keyValues = properties.forKey(LogProperties.KEY_VALUES_SOURCES_PROPERTY)
294                                .ofList()
295                                .map(KeyValuesContributors.Selected::parse)
296                                .or(keyValueSources)
297                                .validateIfError(validator);
298                        validator.validate();
299                        return new Globals(change.value(), ansi.value(), lock.value(), threadLocalMode.value(), opt.value(),
300                                        keyValues.value());
301                }
302
303                /**
304                 * Which kind of lock appenders use. Only appenders with a thread local buffer
305                 * have a {@code synchronized} variant ({@link LogAppender.AppenderType}).
306                 */
307                public enum AppenderLock {
308
309                        /**
310                         * {@link #REENTRANT} before JDK 24, where {@code synchronized} pins a virtual
311                         * thread to its carrier (<a href="https://openjdk.org/jeps/491">JEP 491</a>).
312                         * From JDK 24 each appender uses the lock of the type it requested. The
313                         * default.
314                         */
315                        AUTO,
316                        /**
317                         * No appender uses {@code synchronized}: a requested
318                         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} becomes
319                         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}.
320                         */
321                        REENTRANT,
322                        /**
323                         * Appenders with a thread local buffer use {@code synchronized}: a requested
324                         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} becomes
325                         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}.
326                         */
327                        SYNCHRONIZED;
328
329                }
330
331                /**
332                 * Whether the logging path may use a {@link ThreadLocal}.
333                 */
334                public enum ThreadLocalMode {
335
336                        /**
337                         * Thread locals may be used. The default.
338                         */
339                        ALLOW,
340                        /**
341                         * Nothing in the logging path uses a thread local: appenders with a thread
342                         * local buffer become {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_NEW_BUFFER}, and
343                         * modules that keep context in a thread local, such as SLF4J's MDC, turn it
344                         * off.
345                         */
346                        FORBID;
347
348                }
349
350                /**
351                 * Whether output uses ANSI escape codes, for color.
352                 */
353                public enum AnsiMode {
354
355                        /**
356                         * ANSI is used when the console supports it, see
357                         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.AnsiSupport#isAnsiSupported()}. The
358                         * default.
359                         */
360                        AUTO,
361                        /**
362                         * ANSI is always used.
363                         */
364                        @EnumAlias("true")
365                        ON,
366                        /**
367                         * ANSI is never used, and extensions for ANSI such as JANSI are not
368                         * installed.
369                         */
370                        @EnumAlias("false")
371                        OFF;
372
373                        static AnsiMode parse(String value) {
374                                return switch (value.strip().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)) {
375                                        case "TRUE" -> ON;
376                                        case "FALSE" -> OFF;
377                                        default -> LogProperty.enumValue(AnsiMode.class, value, "true", "false");
378                                };
379                        }
380
381                }
382
383        }
384
385        /**
386         * Accounts for logger names, and which {@link LoggerAPI} vended them, registered via
387         * {@link #registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI, String)}, deliberately without exposing the
388         * accumulated names/APIs themselves: the one supported way to see them is
389         * {@link LogReporter.Section#LOGGERS}/{@link LogReporter.Section#FACADES}.
390         */
391        interface LoggerRegistry {
392
393                /**
394                 * Registers that a logger with this name exists. Idempotent: registering the same
395                 * name more than once has no additional effect. The first time a given name is
396                 * registered this also increments {@link LogMetrics#LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC} on
397                 * {@link LogConfig#metrics()}, so the running total is cheap to observe (e.g. to
398                 * catch unbounded logger name usage) without ever having to size the accumulated
399                 * names themselves.
400                 * @param api which facade this name came through.
401                 * @param loggerName logger name.
402                 */
403                void registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI api, String loggerName);
404
405        }

425        /**
426         * Config Change Publisher. Runtime changes are on when
427         * {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} (or
428         * {@link Builder#changeMode(ChangeMode)}) is {@link ChangeMode#ON}. When on,
429         * {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} + {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger
430         * name, set to a list of {@link ChangeType} or <code>true</code>/<code>false</code>,
431         * chooses what may change per logger. When off, {@link #allowedChanges(String)} is
432         * always empty and {@link #publish()} does nothing.
433         * <p>
434         * Caller info is not a change: {@value LogProperties#CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX} +
435         * {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger name, set to a {@link CallerType} (or
436         * <code>true</code>/<code>false</code>), applies whatever the change mode. It is
437         * resolved independently of {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX}, even for
438         * overlapping logger name prefixes.
439         * <p>
440         * Both accept an enabled group name ({@value LogProperties#GROUPS_PROPERTY}) in place
441         * of a logger name, applying to the loggers the group lists and their children. As
442         * with levels, a logger's own key wins over a group at the same logger name, and the
443         * last group listed wins when a logger is in more than one.
444         */
445        interface ChangePublisher {
446
447                /**
448                 * Subscribe to changes.
449                 * @param consumer consumer.
450                 */
451                public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer);
452
453                /**
454                 * Publish that there has been changes.
455                 */
456                public void publish();
457
458                /**
459                 * Test to see if <strong>any</strong> changes are enabled for a logger - either
460                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} is non-empty or {@link #callerType(String)} is
461                 * not {@link CallerType#NONE}.
462                 * @param loggerName logger name.
463                 * @return true if enabled.
464                 */
465                public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName);
466
467                /**
468                 * Returns what the logger is allowed to change.
469                 * @param loggerName logger name.
470                 * @return which things are allowed to change in the logger
471                 */
472                public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName);
473
474                /**
475                 * The caller info strategy for a logger, resolved from
476                 * {@value LogProperties#CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX}, independently of
477                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} /{@value LogProperties#CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX}.
478                 * Unlike {@link ChangeType#LEVEL}, which is genuinely re-evaluated on every
479                 * {@link #publish()}, this is resolved once when a logger is first created and
480                 * never revisited afterward - it reflects a static per-logger capability, not
481                 * something that changes at runtime.
482                 * @param loggerName logger name.
483                 * @return caller type, {@link CallerType#NONE} if not configured.
484                 */
485                public CallerType callerType(String loggerName);
486
487                /**
488                 * Whether caller info should be computed for a logger at all, regardless of which
489                 * non-{@link CallerType#NONE} strategy.
490                 * @param loggerName logger name.
491                 * @return true if caller info is enabled for this logger.
492                 */
493                default boolean callerInfoEnabled(String loggerName) {
494                        return callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
495                }
496
497                /**
498                 * Whether runtime changes are on for a configuration, set with
499                 * {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY}.
500                 */
501                public enum ChangeMode {
502
503                        /**
504                         * Loggers never change after they are created.
505                         */
506                        @EnumAlias("false")
507                        OFF,
508                        /**
509                         * Loggers allowed by {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} change when
510                         * changes are published.
511                         */
512                        @EnumAlias("true")
513                        ON;
514
515                        static ChangeMode parse(String value) {
516                                String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
517                                return switch (v) {
518                                        case "TRUE" -> ON;
519                                        case "FALSE" -> OFF;
520                                        default -> LogProperty.enumValue(ChangeMode.class, value, "true", "false");
521                                };
522                        }
523
524                }
525
526                /**
527                 * Changing type options.
528                 */
529                public enum ChangeType {
530
531                        /**
532                         * No changes are allowed. Synonymous with <code>false</code> - never actually
533                         * present in a {@link #allowedChanges(String)} result (that case is just the
534                         * empty set); this exists so a single malformed-vs-explicitly-off token can
535                         * be told apart while parsing, and so <code>false</code> is a real,
536                         * documented enum member rather than only a magic string.
537                         */
538                        @EnumAlias("false")
539                        NONE,
540                        /**
541                         * The logger is allowed to change levels.
542                         */
543                        LEVEL;
544
545                        static Set<ChangeType> parse(List<String> value) {
546                                if (value.isEmpty()) {
547                                        return Set.of();
548                                }
549                                var s = EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
550                                for (var v : value) {
551                                        if (v.equalsIgnoreCase("true")) {
552                                                return EnumSet.complementOf(EnumSet.of(ChangeType.NONE));
553                                        }
554                                        var ct = ChangeType.parse(v);
555                                        if (ct == NONE) {
556                                                return EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
557                                        }
558                                        s.add(ct);
559                                }
560                                return s;
561                        }
562
563                        static ChangeType parse(String value) {
564                                String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
565                                return switch (v) {
566                                        case "FALSE" -> NONE;
567                                        default -> LogProperty.enumValue(ChangeType.class, value, "true", "false");
568                                };
569                        }
570
571                }
572
573        }
574

605
606                private Globals.ThreadLocalMode threadLocal = Globals.ThreadLocalMode.ALLOW;

608                private boolean optimize = false;

610                private Set<LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source> keyValueSources = Set

612
613                /**
614                 * Default constructor
615                 */
616                private Builder() {
617                }
618
619                /**

663                /**
664                 * Sets whether runtime changes are on, used when the property
665                 * {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} is absent.
666                 * @param changeMode change mode, default {@link ChangeMode#OFF}.
667                 * @return this.
668                 */
669                public Builder changeMode(ChangeMode changeMode) {
670                        this.changeMode = Objects.requireNonNull(changeMode);
671                        return this;
672                }
673
674                /**
675                 * Sets whether output uses ANSI escape codes, used when the property
676                 * {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_ANSI_MODE_PROPERTY} is absent.
677                 * @param ansiMode ANSI mode, default {@link Globals.AnsiMode#AUTO}.

679                 */

685                /**
686                 * Sets which kind of lock appenders use, used when the property
687                 * {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_LOCK_PROPERTY} is absent.

691                public Builder appenderLock(Globals.AppenderLock appenderLock) {

721                 * Sets the key value sources whose contributors add key values to events, used

731                /**
732                 * Sets service registry
733                 * @param serviceRegistry service registry.
734                 * @return this.
735                 */
736                public Builder serviceRegistry(ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry) {
737                        this.serviceRegistry = serviceRegistry;
738                        return this;
739                }
740
741                /**
742                 * Add to configure LogConfig and ServiceRegistry.
743                 * @param configurator will run on build.
744                 * @return this.
745                 */
746                public Builder configurator(RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator configurator) {
747                        configurators.add(configurator);
748                        return this;
749                }
750
751                /**
752                 * Add properties.
753                 * @param propertiesProvider will run on build.
754                 * @return this.
755                 */
756                public Builder propertiesProvider(RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider propertiesProvider) {
757                        propertiesProviders.add(propertiesProvider);
758                        return this;
759                }
760
761                /**
762                 * Sets the service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
763                 * @param serviceLoader loader to use for missing components.
764                 * @return this.
765                 */
766                public Builder serviceLoader(ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> serviceLoader) {
767                        this.serviceLoader = serviceLoader;
768                        return this;
769                }
770
771                /**
772                 * Sets a default service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
773                 * This call will just call the {@link ServiceLoader} without providing a class
774                 * loader.
775                 * @return this.
776                 */
777                public Builder serviceLoader() {
778                        return this.serviceLoader(ServiceLoader.load(RainbowGumServiceProvider.class));
779                }
780
781                /**
782                 * Configures the builder with a function for ergonomics.
783                 * @param consumer passed the builder.
784                 * @return this.
785                 */
786                public Builder with(Consumer<? super Builder> consumer) {
787                        consumer.accept(this);
788                        return this;
789                }
790
791                /**
792                 * Builds LogConfig which will use the {@link ServiceLoader} if set to load
793                 * missing components and if not set will use static defaults. Registered
794                 * closeables are closed if configuration construction fails.
795                 * @return log config
796                 */
797                public LogConfig build() {
798                        var prePropertiesAlerts = new SwappableLogAlerts();
799                        LogAlerts dumpAlerts = prePropertiesAlerts;
800                        @Nullable ServiceRegistry startupRegistry = null;
801                        boolean startingAlerts = false;
802                        DebugModeType debug = LogProperties.StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES
803                                .forKey(LogProperties.DEBUG_PROPERTY)
804                                .ofString()
805                                .map(DebugModeType::parse)
806                                .or(this.debugMode)
807                                .validateNow(Builder.class);
808                        try {
809                                ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry = this.serviceRegistry;
810                                LogProperties logProperties = this.logProperties;
811
812                                var serviceLoader = this.serviceLoader;
813                                var configurators = this.configurators;
814                                if (serviceRegistry == null) {
815                                        serviceRegistry = ServiceRegistry.of();
816                                }
817                                startupRegistry = serviceRegistry;
818                                if (logProperties == null) {
819                                        List<LogProperties> props = new ArrayList<>();
820                                        for (var pp : propertiesProviders) {
821                                                prePropertiesAlerts.info(LogConfig.class, "Loading properties from "
822                                                                + LogReporter.Reportable.toString(pp, "unknown PropertiesProvider"));
823                                                props.addAll(pp.provideProperties(serviceRegistry, prePropertiesAlerts));
824                                        }
825                                        if (props.isEmpty() && serviceLoader != null) {
826                                                props.addAll(provideProperties(serviceRegistry, serviceLoader, prePropertiesAlerts));
827                                        }
828                                        /*
829                                         * LogProperties.of(List, LogProperties)'s fallback argument is only
830                                         * used when the list is empty, so SYSTEM_PROPERTIES has to be a real
831                                         * member of the list itself to always be included, not passed as that
832                                         * fallback: otherwise it silently disappears the moment any
833                                         * PropertiesProvider contributes anything at all (e.g.
834                                         * rainbowgum-micronaut5's own change mode layer), breaking every -D
835                                         * system property override for such an application with no warning.
836                                         */
837                                        props.add(LogProperties.StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
838                                        logProperties = LogProperties.of(props);
839
840                                }
841                                @Nullable UnusedKeyCheck unusedKeyCheck = null;
842                                /*
843                                 * Reads are recorded for the debug modes that report unused keys, and
844                                 * when logging.alerts.fail fails on a misspelled key's alert: a warning,
845                                 * or an error with logging.alerts.unusedKey=error.
846                                 */
847                                var suggestedKeyLevel = DefaultLogAlerts.unusedKeyLevelOr(logProperties, alertsUnusedKey).level(true);
848                                if (debug.checksUnusedKeys()
849                                                || DefaultLogAlerts.failLevelOr(logProperties, alertsFail).fails(suggestedKeyLevel)) {
850                                        unusedKeyCheck = unusedKeyCheck(logProperties);
851                                        logProperties = recording(logProperties, unusedKeyCheck);
852                                }
853                                /*
854                                 * Built before DefaultLogConfig itself (rather than left for
855                                 * DefaultLogConfig's constructor to create, as before) specifically so
856                                 * buildGlobalResolver below can hand LogAlerts to the global level
857                                 * resolver's alerting wrapper - the global resolver is built before a
858                                 * full LogConfig exists to pull config.alerts() from, so alerts (and
859                                 * metrics, via alerts' own listener wiring) are constructed directly here
860                                 * instead. Capacity and logging.alerts.unobservedErrorsAction both come
861                                 * from logProperties as already resolved above - before any configurator
862                                 * runs, the same as everything else built directly in this method - see
863                                 * DefaultLogAlerts.of(...) for how the two are validated together.
864                                 */
865                                var alerts = DefaultLogAlerts.of(logProperties, alertsFail, alertsUnusedKey,
866                                                debug == DebugModeType.HELP);
867                                LogMetrics metrics = new DefaultLogMetrics();
868                                var levelResolver = this.buildGlobalResolver(logProperties,
869                                                serviceRegistry.findOrNull(LogProperties.class, LevelResolver.OVERRIDE_PROPERTIES_NAME),
870                                                alerts);
871                                var config = new DefaultLogConfig(serviceRegistry, logProperties, levelResolver, alerts, metrics, debug,
872                                                unusedKeyCheck,
873                                                new Globals(changeMode, ansiMode, appenderLock, threadLocal, optimize, keyValueSources)
874                                                        .withProperties(logProperties));
875                                // The config constructor installs the metrics listener before replay.
876                                prePropertiesAlerts.drainTo(alerts);
877                                dumpAlerts = alerts;
878                                if (serviceLoader != null) {
879                                        configurators = new ArrayList<>(configurators);
880                                        findProviders(serviceLoader, Configurator.class).forEach(configurators::add);
881                                }
882                                if (!configurators.isEmpty()) {
883                                        for (var configurator : configurators) {
884                                                alerts.info(LogConfig.class, "Adding configurator: "
885                                                                + LogReporter.Reportable.toString(configurator, "unknown Configurator"));
886                                        }
887                                        /*
888                                         * TODO two-pass config: configurators run after config (and therefore
889                                         * the global level resolver above) already exists, so a configurator
890                                         * that contributes additional property sources or otherwise changes
891                                         * what the level resolver should have seen is invisible to it - the
892                                         * resolver was already built from logProperties as it stood before
893                                         * any configurator ran. A more correct design would run configurators
894                                         * first, then rebuild whatever is purely derived from properties
895                                         * (starting with the level resolver) a second time against the
896                                         * now-fully-configured LogConfig. Not done here - see todo.md.
897                                         */
898                                        RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator.runConfigurators(configurators.stream(), config);
899                                }
900                                /*
901                                 * Deliberately last: alerts already resolved
902                                 * LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction at construction above, but only now,
903                                 * once configurators have had their chance to record alerts and/or
904                                 * register a real Listener, does "should I report/refuse to start"
905                                 * actually mean anything - by construction nothing has had a chance to
906                                 * register one before this point.
907                                 */
908                                // Failure here uses the builder's debug dump, including informational
909                                // context.
910                                alerts.failIfAlerted("building the configuration");
911                                // start() itself reports the backlog before throwing for unobserved
912                                // errors.
913                                startingAlerts = true;
914                                alerts.start(config);
915                                if (debug == DebugModeType.INFO || debug.checksUnusedKeys()) {
916                                        dumpSuccessfulBuild(alerts);
917                                }
918                                return config;
919                        }
920                        catch (RuntimeException | Error e) {
921                                if (debug != DebugModeType.OFF && !startingAlerts) {
922                                        dumpBuildFailure(dumpAlerts, e);
923                                }
924                                if (startupRegistry != null) {
925                                        closeOnFailure(startupRegistry, e);
926                                }
927                                closeOnFailure(dumpAlerts, e);
928                                throw e;
929                        }
930                }
931
932                @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality") // Throwable rejects self-suppression by
933                                                                                                // identity.
934                private static void closeOnFailure(AutoCloseable closeable, Throwable failure) {
935                        try {
936                                closeable.close();
937                        }
938                        catch (Exception | Error closeFailure) {
939                                if (closeFailure != failure) {
940                                        failure.addSuppressed(closeFailure);
941                                }
942                        }
943                }
944
945                /*
946                 * Layers that can list their keys, highest priority first. System properties are
947                 * always listed, even when the properties given do not include them, since a -D
948                 * that nothing reads is exactly what this is meant to catch.
949                 */
950                private static UnusedKeyCheck unusedKeyCheck(LogProperties properties) {
951                        var sources = new ArrayList<UnusedKeyCheck.KeySource>();
952                        var system = LogProperties.StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES;
953                        sources.add(new UnusedKeyCheck.KeySource(system,
954                                        () -> new TreeSet<>(System.getProperties().stringPropertyNames())));
955                        for (var layer : layers(properties)) {
956                                if (layer instanceof LogProperties.Listable listable) {
957                                        sources.add(new UnusedKeyCheck.KeySource(listable, listable::keys));
958                                }
959                        }
960                        return new UnusedKeyCheck(sources);
961                }
962
963                /*
964                 * Preserve composite precedence and mutability while recording every layer.
965                 */
966                private static LogProperties recording(LogProperties properties, UnusedKeyCheck check) {
967                        if (properties instanceof ListLogProperties list) {
968                                var wrapped = java.util.Arrays.stream(list.properties())
969                                        .map(layer -> recording(layer, check))
970                                        .toArray(LogProperties[]::new);
971                                return properties instanceof LogProperties.MutableLogProperties
972                                                ? new CompositeMutableLogProperties(wrapped) : new CompositeLogProperties(wrapped);
973                        }
974                        return check.wrap(properties);
975                }
976
977                private static List<LogProperties> layers(LogProperties properties) {
978                        var layers = new ArrayList<LogProperties>();
979                        if (properties instanceof ListLogProperties list) {
980                                for (var layer : list.properties()) {
981                                        layers.addAll(layers(layer));
982                                }
983                        }
984                        else {
985                                layers.add(properties);
986                        }
987                        return layers;
988                }
989
990                private static void dumpSuccessfulBuild(LogAlerts alerts) {
991                        var events = alerts.dump();
992                        MetaLog.error(LogEventFactory.of(LogConfig.class.getName())
993                                .eventNoArg(Level.INFO, "LogConfig built; dumping " + events.size() + " alert(s)", null));
994                        for (var event : events) {
995                                MetaLog.error(event);
996                        }
997                }
998
999                /* Throwable.addSuppressed rejects self-suppression. */
1000                @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
1001                private static void dumpBuildFailure(LogAlerts alerts, Throwable failure) {
1002                        try {
1003                                var events = alerts.dump();
1004                                MetaLog.error(LogConfig.class, "LogConfig build failed; dumping " + events.size() + " alert(s)",
1005                                                failure);
1006                                for (var event : events) {
1007                                        MetaLog.error(event);
1008                                }
1009                        }
1010                        catch (Throwable dumpFailure) {
1011                                if (dumpFailure != failure) {
1012                                        failure.addSuppressed(dumpFailure);
1013                                }
1014                        }
1015                }
1016
1017                LevelConfig buildGlobalResolver(LogProperties logProperties, @Nullable LogProperties overrideProperties,
1018                                LogAlerts alerts) {
1019                        List<LevelConfig> configs = new ArrayList<>();
1020                        if (overrideProperties != null) {
1021                                /*
1022                                 * Checked first at each step of the logger name, so a group level in the
1023                                 * override wins over a logger's own level from another source.
1024                                 */
1025                                configs.add(ConfigLevelResolver.of(overrideProperties));
1026                                configs.add(GroupLevelResolver.of(new LevelOverrideProperties(overrideProperties, logProperties)));
1027                        }
1028                        configs.add(ConfigLevelResolver.of(logProperties));
1029                        configs.add(GroupLevelResolver.of(logProperties));
1030                        LevelConfig levelResolver = LevelConfig.of(configs);
1031                        var config = buildLevelConfigOrNull();
1032                        if (config != null) {
1033                                levelResolver = LevelConfig.of(List.<LevelConfig>of(config, levelResolver));
1034                        }
1035                        return new AlertingLevelConfig(levelResolver, alerts);
1036                }
1037
1038                private static List<LogProperties> provideProperties(ServiceRegistry registry,
1039                                ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> loader, LogAlerts alerts) {
1040                        List<LogProperties> props = new ArrayList<>();
1041                        for (var provider : findProviders(loader, PropertiesProvider.class).toList()) {
1042                                alerts.info(LogConfig.class, "Loading properties from "
1043                                                + LogReporter.Reportable.toString(provider, "unknown PropertiesProvider"));
1044                                props.addAll(provider.provideProperties(registry, alerts));
1045                        }
1046                        return props;
1047                }
1048
1049                @Override
1050                protected Builder self() {
1051                        return this;
1052                }
1053
1054        }
1055
1056}

1058abstract class AbstractChangePublisher implements ChangePublisher {
1059
1060        /*
1061         * TODO Ideally this would be a concurrent weak hashmap. The reasoning is we may want
1062         * a configuration where SLF4J loggers are not stored in concurrent hash map but some
1063         * sort of GC friendly cache or not cached at all. If they subscribe to changes the
1064         * loggers will never be GCed.
1065         *
1066         * Consequently the functional Consumer interface might not be the best choice.
1067         */
1068        private final Collection<Consumer<? super LogConfig>> consumers = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<Consumer<? super LogConfig>>();
1069
1070        /*
1071         * Same shape as LevelResolver.java's CachedLevelResolver: allowedChanges(name) is
1072         * only ever called once per never-before-seen logger name (RainbowGumLoggerFactory
1073         * caches the resulting Logger forever afterward), so a ConcurrentHashMap here matches
1074         * the exact call pattern that made a ConcurrentHashMap the right tradeoff there too.
1075         */
1076        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, Set<ChangeType>> changesCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
1077
1078        /*
1079         * Sibling to changesCache, not folded into it - CallerType is resolved from its own
1080         * logging.caller.logger.<name> property, independent of logging.change.logger.<name>,
1081         * so it gets its own map rather than a combined per-name struct (one map per
1082         * concern).
1083         */
1084        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, CallerType> callerTypeCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
1085
1086        /*
1087         * Built on first use and again after publish, since the group properties may change.
1088         */
1089        private volatile Loggers.@Nullable Groups groups;
1090
1091        protected abstract LogConfig reload();
1092
1093        protected abstract LogConfig config();
1094
1095        /*
1096         * Only allowedChanges and publishing depend on the mode. Caller info is resolved
1097         * whatever the mode.
1098         */
1099        protected ChangeMode changeMode() {
1100                return ChangeMode.ON;
1101        }
1102
1103        @Override
1104        public void publish() {
1105                if (changeMode() == ChangeMode.OFF) {
1106                        return;
1107                }
1108                changesCache.clear();
1109                callerTypeCache.clear();
1110                groups = null;
1111                LogConfig config = reload();
1112                for (var c : consumers) {
1113                        c.accept(config);
1114                }
1115        }
1116
1117        @Override
1118        public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer) {
1119                if (changeMode() == ChangeMode.OFF) {
1120                        return;
1121                }
1122                consumers.add(consumer);
1123        }
1124
1125        @Override
1126        public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName) {
1127                return !allowedChanges(loggerName).isEmpty() || callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
1128        }
1129
1130        private Loggers.Groups groups() {
1131                var g = this.groups;
1132                if (g == null) {
1133                        g = Loggers.Groups.of(config().properties());
1134                        this.groups = g;
1135                }
1136                return g;
1137        }
1138
1139        /*
1140         * Walks up the logger name like level resolution. At each step the key for that name
1141         * wins over the keys of groups listing that name, and only a Missing value continues
1142         * the walk.
1143         */
1144        private <T> LogProperty.@Nullable Result<T> findForLogger(String prefix, String loggerName,
1145                        Function<LogProperty, LogProperty.Result<T>> resolve) {
1146                var props = config().properties();
1147                var groups = groups();
1148                return LogProperties.findUpPathOrNull(loggerName, path -> {
1149                        for (String name : groups.names(path)) {
1150                                var r = resolve.apply(DefaultLogProperty.ofLoggerKey(props, prefix, name));
1151                                if (!(r instanceof LogProperty.Result.Missing)) {
1152                                        return r;
1153                                }
1154                        }
1155                        return null;
1156                });
1157        }
1158
1159        @Override
1160        public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName) {
1161                if (changeMode() == ChangeMode.OFF) {
1162                        return Set.of();
1163                }
1164                return changesCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
1165                        /*
1166                         * findForLogger walks the logger-name hierarchy (closest match wins) trying
1167                         * each candidate key in turn. A present-but-malformed value is a
1168                         * Result.Error, not a Missing - it stops the walk right there rather than
1169                         * silently falling through to a less specific ancestor's value.
1170                         */
1171                        LogProperty.Result<Set<ChangeType>> result = findForLogger(LogProperties.CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX, n,
1172                                        property -> property.ofList().map(ChangeType::parse));
1173                        if (result == null) {
1174                                return Set.of();
1175                        }
1176                        try {
1177                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
1178                        }
1179                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
1180                                /*
1181                                 * A malformed logging.change.logger.<name> value must not be able to
1182                                 * break logging itself. ConcurrentHashMap#computeIfAbsent leaves nothing
1183                                 * cached when the mapping function throws, so without catching this a bad
1184                                 * property would re-parse and re-alert on every single allowedChanges(n)
1185                                 * call for this logger name, not just once - same amplification risk
1186                                 * CachedLevelResolver guards against for level properties. Fall back to
1187                                 * "nothing allowed to change" and alert exactly once per logger name
1188                                 * instead, since the fallback value is itself cached above just like a
1189                                 * successful parse would be. validateNow's own Missing = failure
1190                                 * semantics are moot here - the lambda above never returns a Missing
1191                                 * result to it in the first place.
1192                                 */
1193                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
1194                                return Set.of();
1195                        }
1196                });
1197        }
1198
1199        @Override
1200        public CallerType callerType(String loggerName) {
1201                return callerTypeCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
1202                        LogProperty.Result<CallerType> result = findForLogger(LogProperties.CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX, n,
1203                                        property -> property.ofString().map(CallerType::parse));
1204                        if (result == null) {
1205                                return CallerType.NONE;
1206                        }
1207                        try {
1208                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
1209                        }
1210                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
1211                                /*
1212                                 * Same reasoning as allowedChanges()'s catch above: a malformed (or
1213                                 * pre-split, e.g. the old "caller" token that used to live in
1214                                 * logging.change.<name>) logging.caller.logger.<name> value alerts once
1215                                 * and falls back to CallerType.NONE, cached, rather than re-parsing and
1216                                 * re-alerting on every call.
1217                                 */
1218                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
1219                                return CallerType.NONE;
1220                        }
1221                });
1222        }
1223
1224}
1225
1226final class DefaultLogConfig implements LogConfig {
1227
1228        /*
1229         * Present only in debug modes that check for unused keys.
1230         */
1231        @Nullable UnusedKeyCheck unusedKeyCheck() {
1232                return unusedKeyCheck;
1233        }
1234
1235        private final ServiceRegistry registry;
1236
1237        private final LogProperties properties;
1238
1239        private final DebugModeType debugMode;
1240
1241        private final LevelConfig levelResolver;
1242
1243        private final Globals globals;
1244
1245        private final ChangePublisher changePublisher;
1246
1247        private final LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry;
1248
1249        private final LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry;
1250
1251        private final LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry;
1252
1253        private final LogAlerts alerts;
1254
1255        private final LogMetrics metrics;
1256
1257        private final LoggerRegistry loggerRegistry;
1258
1259        private final Reporter reporter;
1260
1261        /*
1262         * Registered outputs/appenders, alert listeners, and service registry closeables are
1263         * never reset when a RainbowGum closes, so a second RainbowGum on this config would
1264         * fail on duplicate output names, flush/reopen the first one's closed appenders, and
1265         * lose alert listeners. Ownership and built state change together in one CAS so
1266         * concurrent build() calls cannot both win.
1267         */
1268        private final AtomicReference<@Nullable Claim> claim = new AtomicReference<>();
1269
1270        private record Claim(Object owner, boolean built) {
1271        }
1272
1273        private final @Nullable UnusedKeyCheck unusedKeyCheck;
1274
1275        DefaultLogConfig(ServiceRegistry registry, LogProperties properties, LevelConfig levelResolver, LogAlerts alerts,
1276                        LogMetrics metrics, DebugModeType debugMode, @Nullable UnusedKeyCheck unusedKeyCheck, Globals globals) {
1277                super();
1278                this.unusedKeyCheck = unusedKeyCheck;
1279                this.registry = registry;
1280                this.properties = properties;
1281                this.debugMode = debugMode;
1282                this.levelResolver = levelResolver;
1283                this.alerts = alerts;
1284                this.metrics = metrics;
1285                this.loggerRegistry = new DefaultLoggerRegistry(metrics);
1286                this.reporter = new Reporter();
1287                reportProperties(this.reporter);
1288                this.globals = globals;
1289                this.changePublisher = new DefaultChangePublisher();
1290                /*
1291                 * KeyValuesContributor.of only gets the registry.
1292                 */
1293                registry.put(KeyValuesContributors.Selected.class,
1294                                new KeyValuesContributors.Selected(globals.keyValueSources()));
1295                PostProcessors.registerStandard(registry);
1296                this.outputRegistry = DefaultOutputRegistry.of(registry);
1297                this.encoderRegistry = DefaultEncoderRegistry.of();
1298                this.publisherRegistry = DefaultPublisherRegistry.of();
1299                /*
1300                 * addInternalListener, not addListener: a passive in-process counter nobody has
1301                 * wired an exporter to does not count as "someone is watching" for
1302                 * LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction's purposes - see DefaultLogAlerts's own
1303                 * comment on hasExternalListener. Config alerts is always a DefaultLogAlerts;
1304                 * SwappableLogAlerts is only passed to PropertiesProviders before config exists.
1305                 */
1306                ((DefaultLogAlerts) this.alerts).addInternalListener(event -> {
1307                        switch (event.level()) {
1308                                case ERROR -> this.metrics.errorCounter(event.loggerName(), 1);
1309                                case WARNING -> this.metrics.warnCounter(event.loggerName(), 1);
1310                                default -> this.metrics.infoCounter(event.loggerName(), 1);
1311                        }
1312                });
1313        }
1314
1315        void bind(Object owner) {
1316                acquire(owner, false);
1317        }
1318
1319        void markBuilt(Object owner) {
1320                acquire(owner, true);
1321        }
1322
1323        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality") // owner is a specific builder instance
1324        private void acquire(Object owner, boolean build) {
1325                while (true) {
1326                        var current = claim.get();
1327                        if (current != null && current.owner() != owner) {
1328                                throw new IllegalStateException("LogConfig is already used by another RainbowGum. "
1329                                                + "A LogConfig can only be used by one RainbowGum, even after that RainbowGum is closed. "
1330                                                + "Build a new LogConfig instead.");
1331                        }
1332                        if (current != null && current.built() && build) {
1333                                throw new IllegalStateException("This builder already built a RainbowGum. "
1334                                                + "A LogConfig can only be used by one RainbowGum. Build a new LogConfig instead.");
1335                        }
1336                        if (current != null && (current.built() || !build)) {
1337                                return;
1338                        }
1339                        if (claim.compareAndSet(current, new Claim(owner, build))) {
1340                                return;
1341                        }
1342                }
1343        }
1344
1345        final class Reporter extends DefaultLogReporter {
1346
1347                @Override
1348                LogConfig config() {
1349                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;
1350                }
1351
1352        }
1353
1354        class DefaultChangePublisher extends AbstractChangePublisher {
1355
1356                @Override
1357                protected LogConfig config() {
1358                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;
1359                }
1360
1361                @Override
1362                protected ChangeMode changeMode() {
1363                        return globals.changeMode();
1364                }
1365
1366                @Override
1367                protected LogConfig reload() {
1368                        levelResolver.clear();
1369                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;
1370                }
1371
1372        }

1450final class DefaultLoggerRegistry implements LogConfig.LoggerRegistry {
1451
1452        private final Set<String> loggerNames = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
1453
1454        private final Set<LoggerAPI> loggerAPIs = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
1455
1456        private final LogMetrics metrics;
1457
1458        DefaultLoggerRegistry(LogMetrics metrics) {
1459                this.metrics = metrics;
1460        }
1461
1462        @Override
1463        public void registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI api, String loggerName) {
1464                Objects.requireNonNull(api);
1465                loggerAPIs.add(api);
1466                if (loggerNames.add(loggerName)) {
1467                        metrics.infoCounter(LogMetrics.LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC, 1);
1468                }
1469        }
1470
1471        /*
1472         * Deliberately not on the LogConfig.LoggerRegistry interface itself (see its
1473         * javadoc): DefaultLogReporter downcasts to this package-private type to reach it,
1474         * the same pattern DefaultLogConfig's own constructor already uses to reach
1475         * DefaultLogAlerts#addInternalListener.
1476         */
1477        Set<String> loggerNames() {
1478                return Set.copyOf(loggerNames);
1479        }
1480
1481        /**
1482         * Every {@link LoggerAPI} registered so far via {@link #registerLoggerName}, not just
1483         * {@link LoggerAPI.Standard}: an application-provided {@link LoggerAPI} works too.
1484         * Same downcast-only visibility as {@link #loggerNames()}.
1485         * @return immutable snapshot.
1486         */
1487        Set<LoggerAPI> loggerAPIs() {
1488                return Set.copyOf(loggerAPIs);
1489        }
1490
1491}
